title: ELISA-based protein-PAMP interaction assay
protocol: Incubate aliquots of 100 μl LPS or LTA resuspended in 0.01 M pH 7.4 PBS in a 96-well microtitre plate at room temperature overnight.
Rinse the wells three times with 300 μl of PBS each.
Block the wells with 150 μl of PBS with 2% (w/v) BSA at 37°C for 2 h.
Rinse the wells three times with 300 μl of PBS each.
Add to each well, 100 μl of serially diluted protein (HMC or Hb in 2% BSA) in PBST and incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Rinse the wells three times with 300 μl of PBST each.
Add to each well, 100 μl of primary antibody (rabbit-anti HMC or rabbit-anti Hb), diluted to 1:500 with 2% BSA in PBST and incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Rinse the wells three times with 300 μl of PBST each.
Add to each well, 100 μl of horseradish peroxidase-conjugated goat-anti-rabbit antibody (DAKO), diluted to 1:1000 in 2% BSA in PBST and incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Rinse the wells three times with 300 μl of PBST each.
Add 50 μl of the peroxidase substrate to each well.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Choose a concentration of either HMC or Hb that shows an ELISA-readout (A405) in the linear range.
Incubate the chosen concentration of HMC or Hb with LPS or LTA concentrations ranging from 0 to 200 μg/ml in 2% BSA in PBST at 37°C for 1 hour.
Transfer the reaction mixture to the LPS- or LTA-immobilized microtitre plate.
Conduct the ELISA as described in steps 5 through 13.
The reduction of the readout of HMC or Hb pre-incubated with LPS or LTA, respectively, demonstrates the specificity of the protein-PAMP interaction.
